response.sql: WITH combo AS (SELECT o.recordvault AS order_ref, o.orderflow AS status, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.recordvault, o.orderflow), shares AS (SELECT order_ref, status, record_count, record_count * 1.0 / SUM(record_count) OVER (PARTITION BY status) AS share FROM combo), gaps AS (SELECT order_ref, status, record_count, share, AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY status) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT order_ref, status, record_count, share, share - avg_share AS gap_above_avg FROM gaps ORDER BY gap_above_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The 'order reference' is orders.recordvault, which is unique per order, so each order has exactly one status. Each combination is therefore one order with its status.
A status's 'average share' is the simple mean of the shares of all combinations within that status. It is not weighted.
The gap is share minus average share, with no rounding. Ties at the 10th place are cut arbitrarily by LIMIT.
